label: Meaning of colonization
quiz: What distinguishes colonization from a brief visit?
An outside power establishing continuing authority over people and place
Only a ship arriving for one day
Any exchange between traders
A new name that creates local history
retry: A record shows a passing ship but no continuing authority. What is supported?
Evidence of a visit, not enough by itself to establish colonial rule
Proof of universal colonial control
Proof that all residents consented
Evidence that no community existed before
hard: A map labels a place as a colony without evidence about institutions or actions. What should a learner ask?
How authority was established and maintained in that place
Why the label proves everyone obeyed
Which colour guarantees historical accuracy
Why local evidence is unnecessary

label: Colonial motives
quiz: Which statement describes a motive?
A sponsor sought trade access and political influence
An office was established to issue decisions
Goods were collected from a household
A family had fewer goods after collection
retry: What does identifying a religious aim fail to establish?
That everyone adopted the religion or freely consented to rule
That an aim can be studied historically
That participants could have priorities
That a source can describe a sponsor's intention
hard: An account names an economic aim and calls coercion justified. How should a report respond?
Explain the aim separately from evaluating the method and its effects
Assume wanting wealth makes all force acceptable
Treat the aim as proof of universal consent
Replace the account with invented dialogue

label: Methods of authority
quiz: Which example most directly describes a method?
Establishing an office to issue governing decisions
Wanting more influence
Hoping for profitable trade
Experiencing a later consequence
retry: How should tribute be introduced in this mission?
A required payment, with details needing evidence by place and period
Always a freely chosen gift
The same amount paid by every household in all periods
A complete explanation of every local response
hard: A report labels a required payment a voluntary gift without checking context. What is missing?
Evidence about the requirement, collection and pressure involved
Only a more attractive label
A claim that every payment is identical
An invented statement of everyone's approval

label: Effects and local responses
quiz: Which statement most directly concerns an effect?
A documented consequence for people following a policy
Only the sponsor's original wish
Only the name of a governing office
Only a claim that an outcome was inevitable
retry: Why study household circumstances when examining a payment?
Consequences can vary and need evidence about affected people
All households necessarily had one identical experience
An official's intention reveals every private feeling
A policy name proves every effect
hard: A fictional household record shows fewer goods after a collection. What conclusion stays within it?
That consequence is supported for the example; universal claims need more evidence
All families everywhere had the same loss
No local response could occur
The record proves everyone welcomed the collection

label: Checking reports
quiz: Why should an official's account be examined for viewpoint?
It may emphasize aims while leaving local experiences or enforcement unclear
All official accounts contain every person's thoughts
A source label guarantees universal truth
Viewpoint means every recorded event is false
retry: Which inference goes beyond evidence that an office was created?
Every community freely accepted and obeyed it
An institutional action was recorded
The office can be investigated
The account makes a specific claim
hard: A caption jumps from an institution to universal consent. What is the best revision?
State the institution and ask for separate evidence of reach and responses
Keep both claims because they sound connected
Invent a historical speech to close the gap
Remove all local people from the explanation
